rationale: The child is a brief social regret-and-congratulations letter. C05 is the closest because it congratulates and commends recipients for distinguished work; C08 shares the encomiastic construction “I can think of no one”; and C16 offers personal thanks for a job well done. These are generic expressions of presidential praise, however, not a distinctive shared passage, parallel operative sequence, or adapted administrative mechanism sufficient to establish a material drafting template.

shared_material.child_excerpt: With all of you, I join in warm congratulations to General Marshall.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Chairman and members of the Commission join me in congratulations to you
shared_material.explanation: C05 contains a similar formulation for joining others in congratulations, but this is conventional congratulatory language and the surrounding letters have different structures and purposes.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I can think of no one more richly deserving of this recognition.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I can think of no one with a keener grasp of the problems
shared_material.explanation: C08 shares the phrase “I can think of no one,” but the remainder and function differ, making the overlap too generic to demonstrate templating.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I know that it will never weary of the well-doing that has earned it such an abundance of gratitude and good wishes.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I wish to extend to you my personal thanks and those of the people of the United States for a job well done.
shared_material.explanation: Both praise past service, but C16’s resignation acknowledgment supplies no distinctive language or structure reproduced in the child.
